import pandas as pd

# Source file paths
source_files = [
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_93/training_0.csv"
]

# List to hold loaded source DataFrames
source_dfs = []

# Load each source CSV file with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
for file_path in source_files:
    df = pd.read_csv(file_path, index_col=0)
    source_dfs.append(df)

# Since all source tables have the same schema as the target:
# ['user_id', 'time', 'bet', 'win']
# We can union (concatenate) all source tables vertically.

# Concatenate all source DataFrames
combined_df = pd.concat(source_dfs, ignore_index=True)

# Ensure columns are in the target schema order and types:
# Target schema: ['user_id': string, 'time': string, 'bet': float, 'win': float]

# Convert user_id and time to string explicitly
combined_df['user_id'] = combined_df['user_id'].astype(str)
combined_df['time'] = combined_df['time'].astype(str)

# Convert bet and win to float (they may contain NaNs)
combined_df['bet'] = pd.to_numeric(combined_df['bet'], errors='coerce')
combined_df['win'] = pd.to_numeric(combined_df['win'], errors='coerce')

# The target examples show that NaNs are allowed for bet and win, so no fillna needed.

# Write the combined DataFrame to the target CSV file
output_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_93/target_multisource.csv"
combined_df.to_csv(output_path, index=False)
